questions.question: When checking your tires before a trip, what should you look at?
questions.explanation: Check that your tire pressure is not too low or too high before your trip.

questions.question: What should you pay extra attention to during a winter pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: In winter, make sure your coolant and antifreeze levels are safe.

questions.question: What can a broken exhaust system do?

options.text: Let poisonous fumes into the cab

questions.correctAnswerText: Let poisonous fumes into the cab
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous because poisonous fumes can enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: What should you do to stay alert while driving?

options.text: Eat a heavy meal before starting your trip
Drive with a second person who can help share driving duties

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with a second person who can help share driving duties
questions.explanation: Having a second driver reduces the chance that either of you will drive while tired. You can also stay alert by avoiding heavy meals and keeping the cab cool.

questions.question: When loading cargo, where should you place the weight?
questions.explanation: A vehicle can tip over if its center of gravity is too high. Place cargo weight as low and evenly as possible to prevent tipping.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (like reaching for something), mental (like talking to a passenger), or both (like texting on a phone).

questions.question: What is often found in compressed air?
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. You must drain the tanks regularly.

questions.question: What happens to a vehicle on a downgrade?

options.text: It travels at the same speed as on level ground
It likely swerves to the right

questions.explanation: Gravity causes a vehicle to speed up on a downgrade. Adjust your speed before a hill to avoid using your brakes too much.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand to keep the other hand free
With one hand at a time, alternating hands

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid a crash?

options.text: Braking is always the best option
Swerving may be more effective than braking
Drivers should leave 100 yards between their vehicle and the next

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be more effective than braking
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest choice. You can usually turn to avoid an obstacle faster than you can stop.

questions.question: For a single vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should not exceed ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test, air brake systems should leak no more than 2 psi per minute. If leakage is faster, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: A second conviction for operating a CMV with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.04 percent or higher results in:

options.text: Loss of your CDL for life.
Loss of your CDL for five years.
Loss of your CDL for one year.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loss of your CDL for life.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to operate a CMV with a BAC of 0.04 percent or higher. A first offense results in losing your CDL for one year. A second offense results in losing your CDL for life.

questions.question: After a trip, you should:

options.text: Place the vehicle out of service.

questions.explanation: After a trip, you may need to inspect the vehicle and file a report.

questions.question: If the ABS warning light comes on while driving, it means:

options.text: The ABS has just been activated.
The ABS is not working properly.
The ABS needs to be activated.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow warning lights. When these lights turn on, something is wrong with the braking system. You may have lost ABS on one or more wheels.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Is a major cause of fatal crashes.
Is a good way to reach your destination quickly.
Should only be done on dry roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a major cause of fatal crashes.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed causes many fatal crashes. Never drive faster than the posted speed limit and adjust your speed to match road conditions.

questions.question: When parked on a flat surface, you should:

options.text: Use wheel chocks to stop your vehicle from moving.
Use wheel chocks only after applying the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to stop your vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: Use wheel chocks when parking on a level surface. This is essential to prevent the trailer from moving, especially if the vehicle has no spring brakes.

questions.question: After starting a trip with cargo, you should:

options.text: Inspect the cargo only if it is making noise.
Inspect the cargo only if there is an obvious problem.
Inspect the cargo after 50 miles to make sure it is still secure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inspect the cargo after 50 miles to make sure it is still secure.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before starting a trip, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles to ensure it stays secure.

questions.question: When driving on the expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors for traffic as needed.
Drive on the left side of the lane.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for traffic as needed.
questions.explanation: On the expressway during the skills test, maintain proper lane position, spacing, and speed. Always check your mirrors and surroundings in all directions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a crime that disqualifies an applicant from a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: Certain crimes disqualify you from a hazardous materials endorsement for seven years. These include arson, robbery, and crimes involving dishonesty or fraud. Serious crimes like murder result in a lifetime ban.

questions.question: The suspension system:

options.text: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
Keeps the load at a safe distance behind the driver.
Maintains a safe distance between your vehicle and other vehicles.
Reduces the weight on the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports the vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. Damage to the suspension system is dangerous.

questions.question: A vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) uses a ____ light to warn that the system is not working.
questions.explanation: ABS warning lights are usually yellow. If the ABS is not working, you can still use your regular brakes.

questions.question: To help other drivers see your vehicle:

options.text: Your headlights should be turned off during the day.
Your headlights should be covered with grease.
Your headlights should be used only when it rains.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlights clean. Clean lights produce more light and help other drivers see your vehicle better.

questions.question: You should not use your mirrors to:

options.text: Check how fast you are traveling.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how fast you are traveling.
questions.explanation: Use your mirrors when changing lanes, turning, merging, and making tight maneuvers. Do not use mirrors to check your speed. Use your speedometer for that.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Move quickly before other vehicles enter the lane you want.
Move slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane you want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane you want.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives other drivers time to move or warn you with their horn. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: A cardboard box on the roadway:

options.text: Is not a cause for concern.
May contain a heavy object that could damage your vehicle.
Should be avoided by driving off the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: May contain a heavy object that could damage your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road is potentially dangerous. A cardboard box may look harmless but could contain a hard or heavy object that damages your vehicle.

questions.question: According to the National Sleep Foundation, about ____ of people have driven while sleepy.
questions.explanation: The National Sleep Foundation reports that 60 percent of Americans have driven while sleepy. About 36 percent admit they have actually fallen asleep while driving.

questions.question: To complete an offset back/right parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then back to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, pull straight forward first, then back up to the right. Park completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: Which of these surfaces is the most slippery?
questions.explanation: Wet ice forms when the weather is warm enough to melt ice slightly. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: Header boards:

options.text: Protect the driver from cargo in a crash or sudden stop.
Protect the driver's head when entering the truck cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from cargo in a crash or sudden stop.
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called "headache racks," protect the driver from cargo that moves during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Turn off your turn signal just before starting the turn.
Signal only if vehicles are in front of you.

questions.explanation: Turn on your turn signal well before you turn or change lanes. Keep the signal on during the entire turn. Turn it off after the turn is complete if your vehicle does not have self-canceling signals.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a warning sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Warning signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, repeated yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering the last few miles, missing exits or traffic signs, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, or hitting a rumble strip. Staying within your lane is good driving and not a sign of fatigue.

questions.question: One way to avoid becoming an aggressive driver is to:

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Set realistic expectations regarding travel time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Set realistic expectations regarding travel time.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip ahead of time to allow extra time for traffic delays. This helps you avoid frustration that can lead to aggressive driving. Other ways to prevent aggressive driving include driving at a safe speed, keeping a safe distance from other vehicles, avoiding hand gestures, and keeping both hands on the steering wheel.

questions.question: An example of mandatory emergency equipment is:

options.text: A supply of spare electrical fuses.

questions.correctAnswerText: A supply of spare electrical fuses.
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes at least one fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless your vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles such as reflective triangles.

questions.question: If a vehicle is accompanied by a vehicle inspection report:

options.text: The driver should first inspect the vehicle, then compare their notes with the report.
The driver should first look at the report when completing an inspection.
The driver should not conduct a pre-trip inspection and should rely only on the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver should first look at the report when completing an inspection.
questions.explanation: Always review the inspection report from the previous driver before you start your own vehicle inspection.

questions.question: If pulled over on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Use the taillights to alert other motorists.
Keep your lights off to avoid distracting other drivers.
Set out items from the cab to warn motorists.

questions.explanation: When stopped on the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers and place warning signals to alert other drivers.

questions.question: If unsure if a road is becoming icy, a driver can:

options.text: Open the window and check the front of the mirror for ice.
Try to look at the road closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the window and check the front of the mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: Open your window and feel the front of your side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice has formed on these items, the road surface is likely becoming icy too.

questions.question: In a convex mirror, objects seem ____ than they actually are.
questions.explanation: A convex mirror makes objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: If approaching a railroad crossing that is being approached by a train, you should:

options.text: Try to cross the tracks quickly.
Stop and wait for the train to pass before beginning across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the train to pass before beginning across the tracks.
questions.explanation: Never try to cross railroad tracks ahead of an approaching train. It is hard to judge how fast a train is moving. Stop and wait for the train to completely pass before you cross the tracks.

questions.question: Slippery roadways usually:

options.text: Make it more difficult to stop a vehicle.
Make it easier to stop a vehicle.
Make it easier to drive a vehicle.
Can be avoided by driving at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make it more difficult to stop a vehicle.
questions.explanation: A vehicle needs a longer distance to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Drive carefully when road conditions are slippery.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Other air brake vehicles must have ABS if made on or after March 1, 1998.

questions.question: When making tight turns, a driver should:

options.text: Open the door for a better view.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. You should check them especially carefully when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: When turning quickly to avoid an object in the road, you should:

options.text: Apply your brakes while you steer.
Turn more than needed to give yourself extra clearance.
Turn only as much as needed to miss the object.
Steer and accelerate at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only as much as needed to miss the object.
questions.explanation: Turn only as much as necessary to clear the object. Do not brake while turning.

questions.question: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be:
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers without sides, cargo must be tied down to prevent it from shifting or falling off during transport.

questions.question: When you apply your brakes, the vehicle should:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when you brake, this indicates a brake problem.

questions.question: When traveling slower than 40 mph, how many seconds of following distance should you keep for every 10 feet of vehicle length?
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, maintain at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of vehicle length. At higher speeds, add an additional second.

questions.question: Foundation brakes are located:

options.text: Only at the driver's side wheels.

questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are at each wheel. The most common type is the S-cam drum brake.

questions.question: Your vehicle's final position should be:

options.text: Within five feet of the final position the examiner described.
Within two feet of the final position the examiner described.

questions.explanation: Park your vehicle in the exact position the examiner described. You may fail the basic control skills test if you do not complete an exercise exactly as the examiner instructed.

questions.question: In an emergency stop, you should:

options.text: Lock the wheels and skid to a stop.
Brake in a way that keeps your vehicle in a straight line.
Brake in a way that turns your vehicle.
Expect your vehicle to stop more quickly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake in a way that keeps your vehicle in a straight line.
questions.explanation: Use controlled braking or stab braking to stop in a straight line. This allows you to brake hard while keeping your vehicle straight and able to steer if needed.

questions.question: In cold weather, check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator:
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice buildup in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.
